content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm new to [product_name] and looking to set up a delay timer, such as T005, with a programmable duration. I noticed the VM Mapping feature but I'm unclear on how to properly use it. When I open VM Mapping, I can select my timer T005, but I'm not sure how to adjust other parameters or update the timer value directly from the device panel. Ideally, I'd like to easily change the time setting to values like 2, 10, or 20 seconds. Any guidance would be appreciated. Thanks.

I've attached a straightforward example for setting the timer from the [product_name] display. To change a parameter, you should select the correct message text. Once selected, hold down the ESC key for more than 2 seconds. This brings up a black bar in the input/output field. Use the cursor up/down to navigate between fields. To edit a field, press the OK button (on the [product_name] operator device, press Enter). The black bar becomes a blinking box, allowing you to use the cursor up/down to adjust the value at that position, or left/right to move between positions. When done, press OK again to return to the black bar, where you can select a different field or press ESC to exit.
Thank you, I'll try this out!

analysis.insight_summary: The user was initially confused about how to use VM Mapping in [product_name] software to program a delay timer with an adjustable duration from the device panel. Another user provided step-by-step instructions on how to modify timer parameters using the hardware interface. The guidance resolved the issue, highlighting the need for clearer information and greater accessibility in parameter editing for new users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a straightforward and intuitive method to change timer values—like delay durations—directly from the hardware panel, without complicated steps or hidden options.
